 Mumbai, October 26: Petrol and diesel prices remained unchanged across major Indian cities on Monday, October 26. Petrol was priced at Rs 102.12 per litre in Delhi, Rs 111.21 in Mumbai, Rs 113.51 in Kolkata and Rs 107.76 in Chennai. Diesel rates stood at Rs 95.20 per litre in Delhi, Rs 97.83 in Mumbai, Rs 99.82 in Kolkata and Rs 99.55 in Chennai.    
 Crude oil prices declined in early trade on Monday, October 26, retreating from near six-month highs reached last week, although continued attacks on Saudi Arabia kept concerns over global supplies elevated.   
 US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures fell 2.2% to $101 per barrel while Brent crude futures declined 2.1% to $114.3 per barrel. The decline followed a sharp rally on Friday, when both benchmarks gained nearly $3 amid concerns over potential supply disruptions.   
 Brent crude gained around 6% over the previous week, while WTI advanced 2.3%. The rally was fuelled by Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, with the group claiming strikes on the kingdom’s airport and oil facilities over the weekend. Saudi Arabia said it had intercepted additional missiles and drones on Sunday, while partially resuming operations at its main airport following earlier damage.   
 The latest pullback offers some relief to oil-importing countries such as India, where elevated crude prices can increase import costs, put pressure on the rupee and add to inflationary risks. However, prices remain high, leaving markets vulnerable to further volatility as investors assess geopolitical developments and the risk of supply disruptions.   
 Separately, Saudi Arabia plans to begin storing crude oil in Singapore in the second half of 2027 to strengthen supply-chain resilience. In the US, the Department of Energy authorised the release of 400,000 barrels from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to address a supply disruption at a Louisiana refinery.    
 Check the latest petrol and diesel prices in major cities, including Noida, Gurgaon, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Jaipur and Lucknow.   
 Petrol Prices   
 Petrol prices remained unchanged across major Indian cities and state capitals on Monday, October 26, with New Delhi retailing petrol at Rs 102.12 per litre. In the National Capital Region, prices stood at Rs 102.97 per litre in Gurgaon, Rs 101.96 in Noida and Rs 101.54 in Chandigarh. 
 Among the four major metropolitan cities, petrol was priced at Rs 111.21 per litre in Mumbai, Rs 113.51 in Kolkata and Rs 107.76 in Chennai. Bengaluru recorded a rate of Rs 111.68 per litre, while Bhubaneswar’s petrol price stood at Rs 108.97.   
 Hyderabad continued to have one of the highest petrol prices among the listed cities, at Rs 116.15 per litre, followed by Thiruvananthapuram at Rs 115.49. Petrol was priced at Rs 113.19 per litre in Jaipur and Rs 113.37 in Patna, while Lucknow recorded a rate of Rs 101.86 per litre.   
 There was no change in petrol prices across any of the 14 listed cities, with all reporting zero daily price movement. Retail fuel rates vary across states and cities because of differences in local taxes, including value-added tax (VAT), and other applicable charges.   
 Diesel Prices   
 Diesel prices remained unchanged across major Indian cities and state capitals on Monday, October 26, with the fuel retailing at Rs 95.20 per litre in New Delhi. In the National Capital Region, diesel was priced at Rs 95.64 per litre in Gurgaon, Rs 95.44 in Noida and Rs 89.47 in Chandigarh.   
 Among the four major metropolitan cities, diesel cost Rs 97.83 per litre in Mumbai, Rs 99.82 in Kolkata and Rs 99.55 in Chennai. Bengaluru recorded a diesel price of Rs 99.56 per litre, while Bhubaneswar reported a rate of Rs 100.68.   
 Hyderabad and Thiruvananthapuram recorded the highest diesel prices among the listed cities, at Rs 104.23 and Rs 104.40 per litre, respectively. Diesel was priced at Rs 98.25 per litre in Jaipur and Rs 99.36 in Patna, while Lucknow recorded a rate of Rs 95.36 per litre.   
 There was no change in diesel prices across any of the 14 listed cities, with all reporting zero daily movement. Retail diesel rates vary across states and cities because of differences in local taxes, including value-added tax (VAT), and other applicable charges.
